purpose: Preserve the 2026-08-28 Frankenstein destructive-rewrite counterexample and the engineering constraint it forces. Current authority and exact executable evidence outrank this synthesis record.

observed_counterexample.claim_boundary: Counterevidence against unconstrained whole-file model rewrite safety; not proof that every patch-based edit is safe.

related_authority_failure.observed_signal: Relayed text reopened inbox/provider authority and admitted one Together run despite the current explicit FREE_ONLY/no-paid-fallback task authority.

partial_mitigation_reported.mechanism: Current-file injection plus rejection of rewrites below 50 percent of prior size
partial_mitigation_reported.limitation: A size floor can miss semantically destructive edits that retain most bytes; file length is not semantic preservation proof.

hypothesis.statement: Existing-file modification is safer when the accepted mutation is bound to an exact preimage and bounded patch/diff, with unchanged-region or whole-file postimage invariants checked before commit.

counterhypothesis.statement: A small or hash-bound patch can still introduce severe semantic damage inside the touched region; patch bounding alone is insufficient without tests and task-specific invariants.

successor_constraint: Prefer patch/diff-based modification of existing files over free-form whole-file replacement.
Bind the exact pre-edit file identity before mutation and reject source drift before commit.
When whole-file replacement is unavoidable, require exact preimage plus explicit unchanged-region or equivalent structural invariants; a simple shrink threshold is insufficient.
Run focused semantic regressions for changed behavior and preservation regressions for critical unaffected behavior before promotion.
Keep provider-authored changes from invalid authority lineage quarantined until independent clean non-provider review/re-execution.
Never promote source-guard presence or reported local test counts into Frankenstein/GRID10/HCU/EntityOS runtime credit.
falsifiers: A controlled destructive edit preserving more than 50 percent of the old file must show a size-only guard is insufficient.
A stale-preimage patch must be rejected before commit.
A patch mutating an out-of-scope protected region must be rejected even if the postimage is large and syntactically valid.

A clean current non-provider execution of the preservation guard must bind exact source identity and produce zero provider calls and zero secret lookups before retained component credit is considered.
next_exact_gate: On a clean current non-provider checkout, independently review and execute destructive-truncation/preservation regressions including >50%-size semantic-corruption, stale-preimage and out-of-scope mutation controls; bind exact source identity and prove provider_calls=0 and secret_lookups=0.
